Slop PDF · free, in your browser

Edit the text in a PDF

Fix a typo, a date or a name in a PDF without the original document. Click a line of text, type the new words, and download the corrected file.

Edit a PDF

Watch the Slop PDF tutorial: a free PDF editor in the browser
On YouTube, about one minute.

How to do it

  1. Drop the PDF on the page and open the page you want to change.
  2. Turn on Edit text in place from the Edit menu (Ctrl+E), then click the line of text to change.
  3. Type the new words. They are drawn at the same position, size and colour as the old ones.
  4. Use the Text, Whiteout and Image tools in Edit page to add new text, cover something or add a picture.
  5. Choose Download to save the edited PDF.

The old words are covered with a box in the colour of the paper and the new text is drawn on top. The new text uses the same font family when it is installed or bundled, and otherwise the closest bundled family; the info line tells you which.

Your files stay on this device: Slop PDF runs in your browser, with no upload, no account and no watermark.

Questions

Does the edit change the text inside the PDF?

The old line is covered and new text is drawn over it, so the page reads correctly. On a page read by OCR the words in the hidden text layer are replaced too.

Will the new text match the font?

It is set at the same size and colour, in the same family when that font is available to the app, or the closest bundled one. The panel says which font is used.

Can I edit a scanned PDF?

Run the OCR tool first so the page has a text layer, then edit the recognised words. Without OCR a scan is a picture, and you can only cover and add text.

Can I undo an edit?

Yes. Every change can be undone and redone until you download, and the original file is never changed.
